compiled_state.description:
## Observation
On an S3 ticket store (git-remote-s3 0.4.2), every reconciler pass whose lock remote is S3 fails at lock acquisition. `_ref_lock._push_cas` pushes `<blob-oid>:<ref>` with --force-with-lease; the helper runs `git bundle create` on that bare oid, which git refuses ("Refusing to create empty bundle"), and rebar logs only a truncated generic error. The same blob-plus-lease push writes `refs/reconciler/gate` (set_gate/set_pause) and `refs/reconciler/last-pass` (last_pass.publish), and gate clear / repair-pause cleanup delete the ref, so all of these fail or race on S3. Evidence: .rebar/worktrees/inv-s3-reflock/.rebar/scratch/inv-76869/ (moto and a real scratch bucket, since deleted).

Intent: ADR 0031 (ticket 524d-00fa-66ef-4432) designed a bare-ref CAS proven only on GitHub and local remotes; ADR 0093 and docs/s3-backend.md claim reconcile "works identically" on S3 without a test. On real S3: fast-forward-only pushes from a named ref give one winner; `+` drops the compare; delete has no compare (release racing a steal both succeeded in 2 of 10 rounds).

Related: the PUSH_PENDING hint always says "origin"; two checkouts sharing a tracker can name different sync remotes with no warning.

## Decision (operator, 2026-10-30, option 4)
One mechanism on every remote: each write to a `refs/reconciler/*` ref is a commit whose parent is the tip the writer read, pushed as a plain non-forced fast-forward from a temporary named ref. Release and clear write marker commits instead of deleting. Prove the lock operations in a scratch bucket under the `frontier` AWS profile before landing.

## Plan
1. Chain writes (`_ref_lock_push.py`, called via a new `_ref_lock._cas_write`): wrap the payload blob in a one-file tree (`gate.json` for the gate ref, else `lock.json`, the existing reader convention) and a commit whose parent is the observed tip (root when absent), with a fixed identity and a random nonce. Local: `update-ref <ref> <commit> <observed>`. Remote: push `refs/reconciler/tmp/<uuid>:<ref>` with no `+`, no lease, never a bare oid or delete; drop the temp ref in `finally`.
2. Decide a failed push by re-reading the remote tip: our commit -> success; moved off the observed tip -> CAS mismatch; unchanged -> genuine failure raised with remote, ref and the stderr tail.
3. A legacy blob tip (rebar <= 0.13 on git remotes) cannot be a parent: write over it once through the existing lease path from the named ref; S3 never holds one.
4. Markers older readers understand: release writes `{holder: "", lease_secs: 1, heartbeat_ns: now, fence: fence+1, released: true}` (0.13.x sees an expired lease and steals after 1 s); gate clear writes `{gated_mode: "cleared"}` (0.13.x treats an unknown mode as no gate). `read`, `read_gate`, `read_pause_with_oid`, `clear_gate` treat markers as absent; `acquire` reads the tip, chains onto absent or released, and raises RefLockHeldError on a live lock without pushing.
5. Signatures and contracts unchanged: `acquire`/`renew`/`try_break_if_stale` return the new tip oid; `_cas_advance` stays bool for last_pass; `release` returns True only when our marker landed and still clears the local copy; `_read_blob_bytes` reads `<oid>:<name>`, pinned to the observed oid. Consumers verified unchanged: src/rebar/_commands/_repair_pause.py (cleanup releases GATE_REF by observed oid, then expects `read_pause_with_oid` to return None) and src/rebar/_lib_ops.py (`bridge_pause` -> set_pause/read_pause; `bridge_resume` -> `clear_gate`'s changed bool).
6. src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py: PUSH_PENDING names the configured tickets remote.
7. Docs: amend ADR 0031 (chain, markers, mixed versions; deleting a live holder's ref lets its next renew re-create it); ADR 0093 and docs/s3-backend.md: lock refs work on S3 per the scratch-bucket results, every checkout sharing a tracker must name the same `[sync] remote`, and each S3 push/fetch transfers the whole chain (measured size per update).
8. Tests first on local bare remotes with a recording git shim. Held-out tests that read the raw remote ref as a blob (tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_cli_heldout.py `_remote_blob`, tests/interfaces/facades/test_reconciler_last_pass_heldout.py `_remote_payload`) change to read the payload through the commit and treat the released marker as free, because the remote format changes by decision.
9. Scratch-bucket proof with the real helper: 6 clones x 5 rounds per race; bundle size over 200 updates; bucket deleted after.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A recording git shim shows every remote push from `_ref_lock` uses a `refs/reconciler/tmp/` source, no `+`, and no delete refspec.
- [ ] After acquire, renew, steal, gate set, pause set and last-pass publish, the remote ref's tip commit has the previously observed tip as first parent (root when absent).
- [ ] Two clones racing acquire on an absent ref yield exactly one winner; the loser raises RefLockHeldError.
- [ ] Two clones racing acquire on a released marker yield exactly one winner.
- [ ] A renew racing a steal ends with one owner; the losing renew raises LeaseLostError.
- [ ] A release racing a steal ends with the stealer owning the lock; the losing release returns False.
- [ ] After release, `read()` returns None.
- [ ] v0.13.1's `_decode_blob` decodes the release marker with lease_secs 1.
- [ ] After `clear_gate`, `read_gate()` and `read_pause()` return None.
- [ ] `clear_gate` returns True when it clears an active gate and False when the gate is absent or already a cleared marker, so `bridge_resume` reports changed correctly.
- [ ] Repair-pause cleanup (`_repair_pause`) releases its own pause and then observes `read_pause_with_oid` as None; tests/scripts/graph/test_repair_pause_ownership.py passes.
- [ ] Over a legacy blob tip on a bare remote, renew and set_gate each succeed and leave a commit tip.
- [ ] A rejected push with the tip unchanged raises an error containing the remote's stderr.
- [ ] A rejected push after the tip moved is reported as a CAS mismatch.
- [ ] The PUSH_PENDING line names the configured tickets remote.
- [ ] Scratch-bucket winners per round and bundle size per update are recorded on this ticket, and the bucket is deleted.
- [ ] ADR 0031, ADR 0093 and docs/s3-backend.md describe the chain, markers, mixed-version behaviour, the same-sync-remote rule, and the measured S3 cost.

## Non-goals
Bounding the chain (needs a forced write, which has no compare on S3); changing the helper; CI against real S3.
